title: Rapid and Low-cost Prototyping of Medical Devices Using 3D Printed Molds for Liquid Injection Molding
protocol: Design a to-scale mold master using computer-aided design (CAD) software.
Create a 2D sketch in the Right Plane that specifies the internal and external boundaries of a radial cross-section of the cup-like geometry.
Define sketch dimensions using the "Smart Dimension" tool.
Add sufficient relations between elements of the sketch to ensure appropriate constraints are applied.
Exit the sketch when all geometries are appropriately constrained.
Use the "Revolved Boss/Base" feature to revolve the 2D sketch 360° about the Y-axis to produce a 3D cup-like feature.
Create a 2D sketch in the Top Plane for the external boundaries of a cross-section of the teardrop-like probe handle.
Exit the sketch after completing the design.
Use the "Extruded Boss/Base" feature to extrude selected contours and/or regions from the 2D sketch in the Y-direction.
Start the extrusion at the base of the cup-like geometry.
Extend the extrusion away from the opening of the cup-like geometry.
In a separate CAD file, create a rectangle in a 2D sketch on the Top Plane for defining the rectangular prism solid body.
Ensure the X-dimension of the rectangle is larger than the widest mold master geometry in the X-direction.
Ensure the Y-dimension of the rectangle is larger than the widest mold master geometry in the Y-direction.
Exit the sketch after completing the design of the rectangle.
Use the "Extruded Boss/Base" feature to extrude the region enclosed by the rectangle in the 2D sketch in the Y-direction.
Ensure the extrusion length exceeds the longest mold master geometry in the Y-direction.
Combine the mold master and the rectangular prism to form the complete mold negative.
Import the mold master into the CAD file with the rectangular prism.
Align the mold master such that it is centered and completely encased within the rectangular prism.
Use the "Combine" feature and select the "Subtract" operation type to create the mold cavity.
Round pointed corners and edges using either "Fillet" or "Chamfer" for low-resolution 3D printers.
Define portions of the mold to provide alignment guides for overmolded components if overmolding is desired.
Define parting lines which will cut the mold into several pieces.
Design through-holes for threaded rods and screws to hold the mold pieces together.
Create a rectangular 2D Sketch in the Right Plane that extends from the base of the cup-like geometry to the top of the handle of the probe.
Ensure the rectangle’s width exceeds the end-to-end width of the mold.
Use the "Extruded Cut" feature on the sketch and specify a cut toward the negative X-direction to yield one part.
Specify a cut toward the positive X-direction to yield the other part formed by the bilateral parting line.
Suppress the "Extruded Cut" feature.
Create a radially symmetric parting line by defining a 2D sketch in the Right Plane.
Extend one side of the sketch along the Y-axis.
Extend other edges of the sketch past the mold edges in the radially symmetric portion.
Include lines or curves in the sketch to cut through internal regions of the radial cross-section, creating two or more distinct regions.
Select specific regions from the sketch for a "Revolved Cut" feature to remove undesired parts of the mold.
Complete the revolved cut to yield the desired part by leaving unselected regions intact.
Define through-holes for the mold using the "Hole Wizard" feature.
Create through-holes by defining circular 2D sketches in planes normal to the surface.
Apply the "Extruded Cut" feature to those sketches.
Define a gate in the mold using the "Hole Wizard" feature.
Define a gate by creating 2D sketches in planes normal to the surface.
Apply the "Extruded Cut" feature to define the gate.
Define vents in the mold using the "Hole Wizard" feature.
Create vents by defining 2D sketches in planes normal to the surface.
Apply the "Extruded Cut" feature to those sketches for vent placement.
Suppress or unsuppress the respective "Extruded Cut" or "Revolved Cut" features in the mold design software for each desired mold piece.
Save each mold piece as a .STL file or compatible file type with the desired mesh resolution.
Load the .STL files into the 3D printer.
Print the mold pieces and wait until the job is completed.
Remove any support material on the mold pieces after they have finished printing.
Bring mold pieces together to form the mold cavity while aligning the through-holes.
Slide threaded rods or screws into the through-holes.
Position the components to be overmolded in the mold cavity while assembling the mold pieces.
Apply a small amount of silicone RTV adhesive to temporarily secure the component if there is concern about movement during injection.
Wait 15 min for the silicone RTV adhesive to cure.
Provide firm compression on the mold using nuts on each end of the threaded rods.
Secure the nuts in place by adding an additional nut to each end.
Apply silicone RTV to seal gaps, wait 15 min for curing if necessary.
Seal the mold cavity with a runner or sprue leading into the mold gate.
Insert a barb-to-male luer-lock adapter into the gate of the mold cavity.
Ensure a tight fit of the adapter in the gate.
Connect tubing with barb-to-female luer-lock adapters on each end.
Adapt the exposed female luer-lock adapter on the distal end of the tube to a 50 ml syringe with male luer-lock tip.
Drill two holes in the top cover of the desiccator lid chamber wall.
Install a vacuum rated through-wall pipe fitting in one hole.
Install another vacuum rated through-wall pipe fitting in the second hole.
Use PTFE tape or any other type of pipe sealant on components with pipe fitting connections to ensure air-tight seals.
Use tube clamps on barbed tube adapters/fittings to reinforce air-tightness and prevent tubes from slipping.
Connect the vacuum gauge to one of the through-wall pipe fittings with vacuum rated pipe and tube fittings.
Install a vacuum pressure gauge on the outside of the lid for monitoring chamber pressure.
Install an air-operated syringe adapter on the internal side of the lid at the other through-wall pipe fitting.
Connect the syringe adapter to the through-wall pipe fitting with vacuum rated pipe and tube fittings.
Connect a vacuum rated tee pipe fitting to the external side of the through-wall pipe fitting with an attached air-operated syringe adapter.
On one branch of the tee pipe fitting, connect a compound vacuum/pressure gauge for monitoring inject line pressure.
On the other branch of the tee pipe fitting, connect a vacuum rated three-way L-valve.
Connect one branch of the three-way L-valve to a length of tubing leading to a positive air pressure source using appropriate fittings.
Leave the unconnected branch of the three-way L-valve open for now.
Add tubing connecting one branch of the desiccator's built-in three-way T-valve to a tee tube fitting.
Keep the other branch of the desiccator’s valve exposed to atmosphere for venting chamber pressure.
Connect one branch of the tee tube fitting to a length of tubing connected to a vacuum source.
Connect the other branch of the tee tube fitting to the open branch of the three-way L-valve from step 3.1.5 using appropriate fittings and tubing.
Determine the approximate volume of elastomer needed by examining the mold master CAD file.
Increase this volume by 5% to account for elastomer loss during transfers between containers.
Calculate the amount of Part A and Part B of the elastomer necessary based on the manufacturer’s recommended mixing ratio.
Place a disposable plastic cup on a weigh scale and tare it.
Pour Part A and Part B of the elastomer into the disposable plastic cup.
Add any coloring agents or additives to the cup.
Seal the cup opening by pulling a plastic bag over it and securing with 3-4 rubber bands.
Mix for 2 min with a centrifugal mixer to ensure homogeneous mixing.
If available, mix an additional 1-2 min on the degas setting of the centrifugal mixer.
Prepare the elastomer injection syringe using a female luer-lock cap to seal the bottom of a 50 ml syringe with male luer-lock tip.
Secure the seal with Parafilm and 1 rubber band.
Transfer the elastomer from the plastic cup into the 50 ml luer-lock syringe.
If necessary, use broad strokes to sweep residual elastomer clinging onto the walls of the plastic cup.
Optional: Degas the elastomer after transferring into the syringe in the centrifugal mixer for 30 sec.
Seal the open backside of the 50 ml luer-lock syringe with Parafilm and a rubber band.
Design a custom adapter for the centrifugal mixer in CAD if necessary.
Remove Parafilm and rubber band from the backside of the syringe.
Place the syringe with the open backside in a desiccator and degas for approximately 30 min or until bubbles are eliminated.
Insert the plunger into the backside of the syringe while removing trapped air.
Place a syringe needle sharp side down along the wall of the syringe without touching the elastomer inside it.
Connect the syringe plunger to the exposed female luer-lock adapter on the assembled mold, allowing the needle to release air between the plunger and the elastomer.
Advance the needle and plunger as necessary until there is no visible air column between them.
Remove the syringe needle.
Remove the female luer-lock cap from the syringe containing elastomer ready for injection.
Connect the male luer-lock syringe tip to the exposed female luer-lock adapter on the assembled mold.
Secure the air-operated syringe adapter onto the backside of the 50 ml syringe with male luer-lock tip.
Place both the mold and the attached syringe into the injection chamber.
Place the cover onto the injection chamber to ensure an airtight seal is formed.
Pull the entire system within the injection chamber to a vacuum.
Turn both three-way valves on the injection chamber so that the vacuum source is continuous with the desiccator chamber and the column of air behind the syringe plunger.
Slowly pull a vacuum until approximately -14.5 psi is achieved.
Leave the vacuum on to maintain this pressure.
Turn the three-way L-valve to break continuity between the vacuum source while establishing a connection between the positive pressure air supply and the backside of the syringe plunger.
Gradually ramp up positive pressure from the air supply until at least 25-35 psi is achieved.
Wait until the syringe plunger has reached the bottom of the syringe or until elastomer flows out of the mold vents.
Return the injection chamber back to atmospheric pressure.
Turn off both vacuum and positive air pressure supplies.
Gradually turn the three-way L-valve connected to the air-operated syringe adapter to close it to air supply and open it to the vacuum source.
Turn the three-way T-valve to vent residual pressure in the chamber to atmospheric pressure.
Remove the mold and prepare for elastomer curing.
Open the chamber and remove the mold.
Detach the air-operated syringe adapter from the back of the syringe.
Detach the syringe as well as the tube with two barb-to-female luer-lock adapters.
Place a female luer-lock cap on the exposed male end of the barb-to-male luer-lock adapter attached to the mold gate.
Place the mold in a temperature-controlled oven and cure the elastomer according to manufacturer specifications.
Demold the fully cured elastomer device.
Remove nuts and threaded rods or screws from the mold.
Use a scalpel to gently cut into silicone RTV adhesive if used at parting edges.
Separate the parting edges of the mold with a scalpel.
Cut away extra elastomer material from the device using a scalpel at the gate or vents.
Use a scalpel to remove any flash that may have formed at the mold parting edges.
Clean the molds with wipes and non-destructive solvents such as isopropyl alcohol.
